input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer to Vendor at fifteen percent of annual Fees for each week an invoice is late, triggered by a ten-day payment delay. That is directly contrary to the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and is not saved by the fallback, which permits only a capped early-termination fee. Because the charge compounds weekly without any cap and is triggered by a minor and potentially inadvertent delay, it sits in walk-away territory (it can quickly exceed the remaining contract value and is unenforceable as a penalty in substance despite the label). Nothing else in the Agreement caps it: Section 21.3 confirms payment obligations are outside the liability cap. We have proposed replacing it with customary late-payment interest on undisputed overdue invoices, which reaches the preferred position with a minimal edit while leaving Vendor a proportionate remedy. Service credits or SLA remedies running to Customer are unaffected.

ops.oldText: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
ops.newText: 7.7 If any undisputed invoice is not paid within thirty days of its due date, Vendor's sole remedy is simple interest on the overdue amount at the lesser of one percent per month or the maximum rate permitted by Applicable Law, accruing from the date Vendor gives written notice of non-payment until payment. Customer owes no liquidated damages, penalty, or similar charge under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages payable by us, and 15% of annual Fees per week of delay far exceeds any genuine pre-estimate of loss. We have replaced this with customary late-payment interest on undisputed overdue invoices, consistent with our position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.
proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable liquidated damages in 7.7 with capped late-payment interest.
